title: Would love to get some feedback on my OpenTTD inspired sim
author: Big_Whale_95
selftext:
Hey everyone.   
  
Just launched a demo of my OpenTTD / Transport Fever inspired game.   
You can play it on [https://fabianxr.itch.io/transportit](https://fabianxr.itch.io/transportit) 

Mainly don by Opus 5.5. GPT and Grok did some PR Codereviews (as I should use their sub too) 

Would love to get some feedback from you all 🙌

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
...It does not feel good to play, unfortunately.  
  
I really liked the opening sequence where the world as generated with the little tick box display showing what was being made, so I could follow along... and then the game started, and I attempted to start plopping infrastructure.  
  
The interface is impenetrable. It immediately overwhelms the player with options that have no context, without any sort of logical hierarchy. The game does not communicate what the fundamental pieces are that the player should put down in order to start playing.   
  
If we compare this against OpenTTD, it is trivial for anyone to fire-up OpenTDD and just immediately plop down a functional bus route. Optimizing that bus route is quite challenging, but the act of putting it onto the map is fun and easy. It is immediately intuitive has you construct a bus route, and from there you can iterate on that fundamental gameplay logic to build all other forms of transportation.  


This feels like a trap many games using these tools are running into. The machine is very good at creating a UI, so it perhaps becomes too tempting to just create an overwhelming UI that is brimming with buttons to push instead of building something with function in mind.

replies.author: Big_Whale_95
replies.body:
I see thanks. Just got back into openttd and felt a bit overwhelming to

But I will improve it a bit and add a tutorial. Thanks for sharing your feedback 🙏🏻🙌🏼
